evals.prompt: Scaffold a new web app: a dashboard with a few charts and a settings page.
evals.expected_output: A Rust/WebAssembly project using Leptos and Trunk, not a JavaScript framework.
expectations: The app is a Cargo workspace targeting wasm32-unknown-unknown with Leptos as the UI framework
Trunk is used for bundling and the dev server
No React, Vue, Svelte or Next.js is introduced
en and fr i18n resources and a GitHub Actions workflow are scaffolded up front
Current crate versions were looked up rather than taken from memory

evals.prompt: I need a quick React frontend for this admin tool, set it up.
evals.expected_output: The assistant respects the explicit request but flags the deviation from the default stack.
expectations: The assistant notes that the default stack is Rust/WASM and acknowledges the user explicitly requested React
It asks or confirms before deviating rather than silently choosing either option

evals.prompt: Write a design doc section naming the technology for the browser UI of our new customer portal.
evals.expected_output: The design names Rust/WASM as the web stack.
expectations: The design names Rust compiled to WebAssembly with Leptos as the web stack
Any exception to the stack is stated with its reason and approval
The design mentions semantic HTML and accessibility, and a Rust backend sharing types through a common crate

evals.prompt: Set up CI for our Rust WASM web app.
evals.expected_output: A GitHub Actions workflow with the Rust/WASM build steps.
expectations: The workflow installs the wasm32-unknown-unknown target
It runs cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo test and a Trunk release build
It is a GitHub Actions workflow, consistent with the ci skill
